nodes.label: Generic App
nodes.description: Any Android application receiving pointer events via onTouchEvent() or onGenericMotionEvent(). Handles mouse, stylus, and touchpad input through the View hierarchy.

nodes.label: PointerCapture App
nodes.description: Application that requests pointer capture mode (e.g., games, CAD tools). Receives raw relative mouse deltas via requestPointerCapture() instead of absolute screen coordinates.

nodes.label: AccessibilitySvc
nodes.description: Accessibility service that can intercept, observe, and inject input events globally. Used by screen readers, switch access, and assistive technology applications.

nodes.label: InputManager
nodes.description: Top-level Java API for querying available input devices, registering device change listeners, adjusting pointer speed, and injecting synthetic events (requires permission).

nodes.label: InputDevice
nodes.description: Describes a physical input device's capabilities: source types (mouse, touchpad, stylus), reported axes (X, Y, pressure, tilt, scroll), and button state.

nodes.label: MotionEvent
nodes.description: Immutable event object carrying pointer coordinates, pressure, tool type (finger/mouse/stylus/eraser), action code, and historical samples for a single pointer interaction.

nodes.label: PointerIcon
nodes.description: Represents the visual cursor shape for mouse and touchpad input. Applications set per-View icons via setPointerIcon(); the framework composites the final cursor overlay via SurfaceFlinger.

nodes.label: ViewRootImpl
nodes.description: Root of the View hierarchy for a window. Owns the InputChannel socket endpoint, receives MotionEvents from InputDispatcher, and dispatches them down the View tree.

nodes.label: InputManagerSvc
nodes.description: System service (runs in system_server) that bootstraps InputFlinger, manages pointer icon resources, applies screen-size/rotation transforms, and serves as the Binder endpoint for Java InputManager clients.

nodes.label: InputReader
nodes.description: InputFlinger component that continuously reads raw input_event structs from /dev/input/eventX via EventHub. Applies per-device mappers (PointerInputMapper, TouchInputMapper, KeyboardInputMapper) to produce cooked InputEvents.

nodes.label: InputClassifier
nodes.description: Middleware pipeline stage between InputReader and InputDispatcher. Delegates to the IInputProcessor HAL for ML-based palm rejection and gesture classification, then forwards classified events downstream.

nodes.label: InputDispatcher
nodes.description: Receives classified events from InputClassifier, performs focus-based window targeting via WindowManagerService, tracks ANR timeouts, and delivers events to apps through InputChannel socket pairs.

nodes.label: PointerController
nodes.description: Manages the on-screen mouse cursor position, acceleration, pointer speed, and fade-out animation. Communicates with SurfaceFlinger to composite the cursor sprite layer above all app content.

nodes.label: IInputProcessor
nodes.description: AIDL interface (Android 13+) for HAL-backed input event classification. Vendor ML models implement this interface to label events as TOOL_TYPE_PALM or adjust touch classifications for device-specific accuracy.

nodes.label: IInputClassifier
nodes.description: Legacy HIDL/AIDL interface (Android 10–12) for classifying touch contacts as palm touches. Superseded by IInputProcessor in Android 13 but still supported for backward compatibility.

nodes.label: Default Processor
nodes.description: AOSP reference IInputProcessor implementation that passes events through unmodified. OEMs and SoC vendors replace this with ML-based implementations for palm rejection and stylus pressure calibration.

nodes.label: Vendor Input HAL
nodes.description: SoC/OEM-specific input processor implementing IInputProcessor. Provides on-device ML palm rejection, high-accuracy stylus classification, or touchpad gesture recognition tailored to the device's sensor hardware.

nodes.label: evdev
nodes.description: Linux input event interface driver. Exposes /dev/input/eventX character devices that multiplex input_event structs from all registered input devices. Consumed by EventHub inside InputReader.

nodes.label: HID Core
nodes.description: Generic HID kernel subsystem. Parses HID report descriptors, maps HID usage codes to Linux input event codes, and provides transport-agnostic APIs for USB, Bluetooth, and I2C HID drivers.

nodes.label: USB HID Driver
nodes.description: USB transport driver for HID-compliant devices (wired mice, USB touchpads). Submits USB interrupt-transfer URBs to the USB core and feeds received HID reports to hid-core for decoding.

nodes.label: I2C-HID Driver
nodes.description: I2C transport driver for built-in precision touchpads (Microsoft PTP) and pointing sticks. Reads HID reports over the I2C bus via interrupt-driven transfers and feeds them to hid-core.

nodes.label: hid-multitouch
nodes.description: HID multitouch personality driver. Parses MT-A/MT-B protocol touch contact reports, tracks contact IDs across frames, and emits ABS_MT_* events for multi-finger touchpad and stylus input.

nodes.label: USB Mouse
nodes.description: Wired USB HID mouse. Reports relative X/Y delta, button clicks, and scroll wheel over USB interrupt transfers at 125–8000 Hz depending on the device's polling rate.

nodes.label: Bluetooth Mouse
nodes.description: Bluetooth Classic or BLE HID-over-GATT mouse. Delivers button and relative motion reports over the Bluetooth HID profile; handled by the btusb/hid-bluetooth kernel driver chain.

nodes.label: Touchpad (I2C)
nodes.description: Capacitive multitouch touchpad connected over I2C (e.g., Synaptics, ALPS, Elan). Implements Microsoft Precision Touchpad (PTP) HID descriptor for hardware-assisted palm rejection and gesture support.

nodes.label: Stylus/Digitizer
nodes.description: Active electromagnetic stylus (e.g., Wacom EMR, USI 2.0). Reports absolute X/Y position, pressure (up to 4096 levels), tilt angle, and barrel button state via a dedicated digitizer controller.

nodes.label: Trackball
nodes.description: Optical or mechanical trackball. Reports relative ball motion and button clicks as standard HID relative mouse events; uses the same usbhid/hid-core kernel path as a conventional mouse.
